status_summary: Executive Order 14168, signed 2025-01-20 and published 2025-01-30, requires agency forms that ask about sex to offer only male or female without requesting gender identity and directs removal of materials that promote what it calls gender ideology, but it does not itself end any data collection. On 2025-02-25 a CDC spokesperson told STAT that CDC would stop processing transgender identity data to comply with the order and that the Youth Risk Behavior Survey was being modified, while sexual orientation data would continue to be processed. CDC's 2024 BRFSS data page (last updated 2025-09-17) says the dataset was modified to comply with the President's executive orders, with some questions removed, without naming them, while the 2025 standard high school YRBS questionnaire posted on cdc.gov still includes a question asking whether the student is transgender. A September 2026 report on the 2025 YRBS says the shorter national report omitted several topics found in earlier reports, so implementation is partial and varies by survey.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14168 signed; it requires agency forms that ask about sex to offer only male or female and not to request gender identity (published 2025-01-30).
CDC tells a health news outlet that it will stop processing transgender identity data to comply with the executive order; sexual orientation data is unaffected.

CDC's 2024 BRFSS data page, last updated this date, states that the dataset was modified to comply with the President's executive orders and that some questions were removed; it does not name the removed questions.

title: End CDC collection of gender identity data
uncertainties: The CDC decision to stop processing transgender identity data rests on one outlet quoting a CDC spokesperson; no CDC notice announcing it was found, and a Federal Register search for CDC documents on gender identity since 2025-01-20 returned none. The 2025 standard high school YRBS questionnaire read on cdc.gov on 2026-10-18 is undated beyond its year and still asks whether the student is transgender, so the 2025 instrument appears to have collected the item even if CDC stopped processing it. The 2024 BRFSS data page says questions were removed to comply with executive orders but does not name them. A Federal Register notice citing the order for removing sexual orientation and gender identity questions was found for AHRQ's MEPS survey, not for a CDC survey, and is not used here. The court order restoring webpages in February 2025 is known only from secondary reporting.
